notes:
Summary:
- Fintech startup (quant-driven market-making) building low-latency decisioning layer. Primary ask: sub-30ms p99 inference for short prompt templates used in order routing and risk checks.
- Very cost sensitive at scale; want to compare unit economics hosted vs dedicated vs private. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching/caching/quantization) to hit both latency and cost targets.

Workload & requirements (from SE call):
- Workload: micro-prompts (10-60 tokens), heavy synchronous traffic during market hours, average QPS 2.5k, peak 6k for short windows.
- Targets: p50 < 5ms, p95 < 18ms, p99 < 30ms end-to-end from service gateway to token output across trading region.
- Throughput/cost sensitivity: aim to keep per-10k-requests cost below $12 after optimizations.
- Models: prefer smaller, quantizable transformer variants (8B-16B) with 4-bit quantization option; need fallback to cheaper 4-bit model when capacity constrained.
- Routing/fallback: multi-tier routing (dedicated pool primaries, fallback to shared-hosted cheap variants).
- Caching/batching constraints: minimal artificial batching allowed (latency sensitive) but strong interest in prefix/KV caching for repeated prompt prefixes and conversation state reuse. Need cache hit metrics and warm/cold behavior.
- Security/compliance: must support SSO/SAML, KMS for keys, audit logs turned on, and EU data residency for European trading desk. CISO requests POA for on-prem evaluation (air-gapped POC).

Perf bench specifics requested from Redwood:
- End-to-end p50/p95/p99 with 95% confidence; cold cache vs warm cache; single-request latency vs micro-batch (2-8) tradeoffs.
- Memory/KV cache hit-rate impact on latency and token cost.
- Quantized kernel perf for 4-bit and 8-bit variants on A100-like and first-party inference HW.
- Cost projection with recommended batching/caching/quantization knobs.

Recent timeline:
- 2025-11-05: inbound trial signup, self-serve API test (low traffic).
- 2025-11-18: discovery call (Maya Chen, Rajat) - high-level perf targets, legal intro. Fireflies FF-2026-01-15-FTL-DISCOVERY referenced.
- 2026-01-12: SE deep-dive (Rajat) - provided sample traffic trace and prompt templates.
- 2026-01-22: Submitted security questionnaire draft; CISO asked for SOC2 evidence and KMS integrations.
- 2026-02-02: Requested Redwood perf bench for Dedicated hardware (RDW-8421).
- 2026-02-10: Perf review call, preliminary numbers show p50 ~6ms warm, p99 ~42ms; Redwood suggested KV cache tweaks and quantization profile changes (FF-2026-02-10-FTL-PERF-REVIEW).
- 2026-02-20: Internal procurement prep; asked for formal pricing for 3-node reserved cluster and on-prem POC pathway.

Quotes / customer voice:
- "We need determinism at market open — anything beyond 30ms p99 risks order slippage." — Head of SRE
- "If you can show consistent 20-30% cost savings with quantization and caching without compromising p99 SLA, we can onboard Dedicated." — VP of Engineering

Open items / next steps:
- Redwood to run full Dedicated perf benchmark with matching production traces (SE to schedule cluster window).
- Deliver quantified cost model (per-10k-requests) with and without caching.
- Security: provide SOC2, KMS architecture note, and plan for air-gapped POC.
- Procurement: finalize reserved node pricing after bench results.
